The stay in India of Afanasy Nikitin, a merchant from Tver in Russia, who lived in the Bahmani Sultanate of the Deccan for about three years around 1469 to 1472. His notes are the first Russian account of India.

He set out to trade down the Volga, was robbed near Astrakhan, and kept going through Persia. He crossed the Arabian Sea to Chaul on India's west coast with a stallion he hoped to sell, and lived in the Bahmani capital Bidar. He described the sultan's court, the great armies and elephants, Hindu temples and pilgrimages, the food and the poverty, and his own struggle to keep his faith among Muslims and Hindus.

He came home by Persia and the Black Sea, but died near Smolensk in 1475 before reaching Tver. His Journey Beyond Three Seas (the Caspian, Arabian and Black seas) reached India a generation before Vasco da Gama, by land and sea.
